subject: Time to first detection with time unit as replicate instead of site

messages.author: edc716aa20496f25
messages.subject: Time to first detection with time unit as replicate instead of site
parts:
Previously there was discussion on time to first detection relating to ttfd over replicated sites during a single time period. We are interested in the rate of incursion of foxes into a rock wallaby colony where we know foxes are present, occupancy=1. We use N cameras around the colony to detect foxes. So I am thinking we do not need replicate sites/cameras but instead replicate time units (i.e. 12 months/units within a 1 year sampling period). We consider N cameras to be a single detector and the first detection at any camera within a time unit is a data point. The analysis remains the same but site=time unit and detection is across time units not sites.
The aim is to estimate average incursion rate over the sampling period. Does this make sense or do people think it's twaddle?
